Missing scene: a person in blue stopped by and gave灵芝to 神农，神农felt better after eating灵芝
Missing scene: another person in brown came by and had a conversation with 神农
Missing scene: 神农takes record of灵芝and夹竹桃
Wrong information: “他最喜欢吃花，除了夹竹桃以外，什么都花想吃。” -- This says 神农 does not want to eat 夹竹桃, but in the story he tries 夹竹桃.
Wrong information: “古代时候，人不知道他们能吃什么植物，常常一吃就死。” -- The story says people often became sick after eating some plants, not that they usually died.
Wrong information: “一吃就开始死。” -- After trying 夹竹桃, 神农 faints in the story; he does not start dying.

scenes.text: 在古代，很多医生不知道怎么用药。所以他们找到了很多植物对药。神农先看到很多病人，他们吃很多植物对药。但是我觉得他们的吃的植物，让他们病人。神农觉得这个植物可能特别是毒。所以他想找一个植物对药，他们可以吃对药。正好，他找到了一把花，他想把花放在茶里，对药。

corrections.before: 他们找到了很多植物对药
corrections.after: 他们找到了很多能当药的植物
corrections.explanation: Use 当药 for plants that can be used as medicine. 对药 is not the correct expression here.

corrections.before: 神农先看到很多病人
corrections.after: 有一个医生叫神农，他先看到了很多病人
corrections.explanation: When a character appears for the first time, introduce who they are, not only their name. 看见 is a completed event here, so say 看到了.

corrections.before: 他们吃很多植物对药
corrections.after: 他们把很多植物当药吃了
corrections.explanation: Say 把植物当药吃, meaning “eat plants as medicine.” 对药 is not used for “as medicine.”

corrections.before: 但是我觉得他们的吃的植物，让他们病人
corrections.after: 但是我觉得他们吃的植物让他们生病了
corrections.explanation: Use 他们吃的植物, without 的 after 他们. To say that something causes illness, say 让他们生病了.

corrections.before: 这个植物可能特别是毒
corrections.after: 有一种植物可能特别有毒
corrections.explanation: 这个植物 is unclear because no particular plant has been introduced yet, so introduce it as 有一种植物. Say 特别有毒, not 特别是毒.

corrections.before: 所以他想找一个植物对药，他们可以吃对药
corrections.after: 所以他想找一种植物给病人当药吃
corrections.explanation: Use 当药 to mean “as medicine,” and 一种植物 for one kind of plant. 病人 makes clear who will eat the medicine; 他们 is unclear here.

corrections.before: 正好，他找到了一把花，他想把花放在茶里，对药
corrections.after: 正好，他找到了一把花，想把花放在茶里做药
corrections.explanation: When the same person does two actions in one sentence, omit the second 他. Also, use 做药, not 对药, for making medicine.

expressiveness.where: 在古代，很多医生不知道怎么用药
expressiveness.idea: You could explain that people became ill after eating poisonous plants, showing why this was a serious problem.
expressiveness.example: 很多人吃了有毒的植物，常常生病。

expressiveness.where: 神农先看到很多病人
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shen Nong’s concern when he saw the sick people.
expressiveness.example: 他觉得很难过，也很担心。

scenes.encouragement: You clearly introduce the problem at the beginning of the story: doctors did not know which plants could be used as medicine. You also show Shen Nong’s goal of finding plants that people could safely use.

scenes.text: 他不知道如果这把花对你的身体好，这就要看如果这把花毒不毒了。神农想找别的植物，但是这很麻烦。正好，他找到了别的花。他一吃花，很快就生病了。他的肚子疼死了。神农不知道他吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃。

corrections.before: 他不知道如果这把花对你的身体好，这就要看如果这把花毒不毒了
corrections.after: 他不知道这把花对人的身体好不好，这要看有没有毒
corrections.explanation: Do not use 如果 after 不知道 or 要看 when asking whether something is true. Use a yes-or-no form such as 好不好 or 有没有毒; 了 is not used for this state question.

corrections.before: 神农不知道他吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃
corrections.after: 神农不知道该不该吃灵芝或者夹竹桃
corrections.explanation: The subject is already 神农 in this sentence, so do not repeat it with 他. Use the zero form, and 该不该 shows that he is deciding whether to eat the plants.

vocabulary_suggestions.note: “困难” more clearly emphasizes that finding other plants is hard to do, while “麻烦” can also mean bothersome.

expressiveness.where: 正好，他找到了别的花
expressiveness.idea: You could describe the flower so the reader can picture what Shennong sees.
expressiveness.example: 那朵花是黄色的，像星星一样。

expressiveness.where: 他的肚子疼死了
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shennong’s fear when the pain becomes very strong.
expressiveness.example: 他想：我会死吗？

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show the cause-and-effect sequence: Shennong eats the flower, then quickly becomes ill and has a stomachache. You also include his uncertainty about whether he ate 灵芝 or 夹竹桃, which gives the scene suspense.

scenes.text: 别的人给了神农一个灵芝。这个植物可以让神农更好。比方说，他会觉得更健康。吃灵芝以后，他可以再走。现在他觉得更好。最后，神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药。这些植物让神农很高兴。神农想跟很多人分享他的新药。

corrections.before: 别的人给了神农一个灵芝
corrections.after: 有一个人给了神农一个灵芝
corrections.explanation: 别的人 means people other than a person or group already mentioned, but there is no such person or group here. Introduce this new person with 有一个人.

corrections.before: 比方说，他会觉得更健康
corrections.after: 他会觉得更健康
corrections.explanation: 比方说 means “for example,” but this sentence is not giving an example. It directly states the result, so delete 比方说.

corrections.before: 吃灵芝以后
corrections.after: 吃了灵芝以后
corrections.explanation: Eating the lingzhi is completed before the later action of being able to walk again. Use 了 with 吃 to show that the eating has finished.

corrections.before: 最后，神农找到了很多植物，他可以用对药
corrections.after: 最后，神农找到了很多植物，可以用来做药
corrections.explanation: 神农 is already the subject in this sentence, so do not repeat 他. 用对药 is not a Chinese verb phrase; 用来做药 means “use them to make medicine.”

vocabulary_suggestions.note: “好多了” more vividly shows that his condition improved a lot after eating the lingzhi.

expressiveness.where: 现在他觉得更好
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shennong’s thought that he is relieved because he can continue walking and looking for plants.
expressiveness.example: 他想：“我可以再找植物了！”

expressiveness.where: 神农想跟很多人分享他的新药
expressiveness.idea: You could add a short line of speech to show that he wants to help other people learn which plants are medicine.
expressiveness.example: 他说：“这些植物可以做药！”

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show the sequence of Shennong receiving lingzhi, feeling better, and being able to walk again. You also give the scene a strong ending by showing that he wants to share his new medicine with many people.

content: Missing scene: 神农found茶and took a record
Need to add: The flower is 夹竹桃, and 神农 faints.
Missing scene: another person in brown came by and had a conversation with 神农
Missing scene: 神农takes record of灵芝and夹竹桃
Wrong information: “神农不知道他吃不吃灵芝或者夹竹桃。” -- In the story, 神农 does eat 夹竹桃; it is the plant that makes him faint.

scenes.text: 古代的时候有一个人叫神农。他需要当上医，一看别的人就想帮助他们。但是，他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药。神农听说一个远远的地方有一种植物，什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好。神农三个月走去，找到有植物的地方，他看到一个很漂亮的植物，又香又好看。

corrections.before: 他有一个问题，他不知道什么东西能做药
corrections.after: 他有一个问题，不知道什么东西能做药
corrections.explanation: The second 他 refers to 神农 again in the same sentence. After the subject has already been mentioned, omit the repeated pronoun.

corrections.before: 什么病人吃都会觉得身体更好
corrections.after: 什么病人吃了都会觉得身体更好
corrections.explanation: Eating happens before the patient feels better, so 吃 needs 了 to show that this action is completed.

corrections.before: 神农三个月走去
corrections.after: 神农走了三个月
corrections.explanation: A duration such as 三个月 comes after the action verb. Use 了 with 走 because the three-month journey was completed.

corrections.before: 找到有植物的地方
corrections.after: 找到了有植物的地方
corrections.explanation: Finding the place is a completed action in the story, so 找到 needs 了.

expressiveness.where: 他看到一个很漂亮的植物，又香又好看
expressiveness.idea: You could add the flowers’ yellow, star-like appearance to make the place easier to picture.
expressiveness.example: 那儿开着黄色的、像星星一样的花。

scenes.encouragement: You clearly introduce Shennong’s wish to help sick people and the problem he needs to solve. You also give the plant sensory detail by saying that it is fragrant and pretty.

scenes.text: 他觉得，这种一定是做药的花。原来他想错了。吃了以后，神农快生病。 这时一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农，快给他一种红的灵芝。神农吃了以后，他没有病，想起来以前一个人告诉他，灵芝对身体有好处。

corrections.before: 吃了以后，神农快生病
corrections.after: 吃了以后，神农很快生病了
corrections.explanation: 很快 means that the action happened soon. Use 了 because getting sick is a completed event in the story.

corrections.before: 快给他一种红的灵芝
corrections.after: 很快给了他一种红的灵芝
corrections.explanation: Use 很快, not 快, to mean “quickly” in this statement. Give the last verb in this completed series of actions the particle 了.

corrections.before: 神农吃了以后，他没有病
corrections.after: 神农吃了以后，没有病
corrections.explanation: When the subject is the same within one sentence, Chinese normally omits the repeated pronoun. 神农 is already the subject, so do not add 他.

vocabulary_suggestions.phrase: 一个穿着蓝色衣服的人帮神农
vocabulary_suggestions.new_phrase: 一个穿着蓝色衣服的人救神农
vocabulary_suggestions.note: “救” is more precise because the man helps Shennong when he is ill.

expressiveness.where: 他觉得，这种一定是做药的花
expressiveness.idea: You could describe the flower’s yellow, star-like appearance to make the scene more vivid.
expressiveness.example: 花是黄色的，像星星一样。

expressiveness.where: 神农吃了以后，他没有病
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shennong’s thanks to show his relief after the medicine helps him.
expressiveness.example: 他对那个人说：“谢谢你！”

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show the important change from thinking the flower was medicine to realizing he was wrong. You also connect the lingzhi to information Shennong had heard before, which makes the story flow well.

scenes.text: 啊，他怎么忘记了？他把灵芝放在包里。一回家就告诉别人。他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上。所以人们都知道，那红灵芝对身体好处。

corrections.before: 他找到药以后他写下怎么做药在书上
corrections.after: 他找到药以后，在书上写下了怎么做药
corrections.explanation: A place phrase with 在 comes before the verb in Chinese, so say 在书上写下. Since the writing was completed, 写下 takes 了.

corrections.before: 那红灵芝对身体好处
corrections.after: 那种红灵芝对身体有好处
corrections.explanation: Use a measure word such as 种 after 那 when referring to a type of 灵芝. 好处 needs 有 here: 对身体有好处 means “to be good for the body.”

expressiveness.where: 他把灵芝放在包里
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shen Nong’s relieved thought when he remembers that he brought the lingzhi home.
expressiveness.example: 他想：“还好，我把灵芝带回来了。”

expressiveness.where: 一回家就告诉别人
expressiveness.idea: You could add a short line of speech to show what he tells people about the lingzhi.
expressiveness.example: 他说：“灵芝对身体有好处，可以做药！”

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show the order of events with “一回家就” and use “所以” to explain the result. You also connect this ending well to Shen Nong sharing his discovery with other people.

content: Need to add: People do not know which plants are safe to eat, and people get sick after eating some plants.
Missing scene: 神农found茶and took a record
Need to add: The plant is 夹竹桃, and 神农 faints after eating it.
Need to add: A record of both 灵芝 and 夹竹桃, especially 夹竹桃
Wrong information: “吃了以后，神农快生病。” -- In the story, 神农 eats 夹竹桃 and faints; this changes it to nearly becoming sick after an unnamed plant.

scenes.text: 古代的时候，有很多人不知道什么植物能吃，什么植物不能吃。有很多人吃植物以后就吃坏肚子了，因为他们吃了毒。那个时候，有一个老人叫神农，他什么植物都觉得好吃，不怕生病，不怕毒。他希望别人也可以吃好吃的植物。可是他知道，如果他们还怕吃毒，不会吃他喜欢的植物。

corrections.before: 古代的时候
corrections.after: 在古代
corrections.explanation: Use 在古代 to say “in ancient times.” 古代的时候 is not the usual expression here.

corrections.before: 什么植物能吃，什么植物不能吃
corrections.after: 什么植物是能吃的，什么植物是不能吃的
corrections.explanation: When saying which plants are edible and which are not, use 是能吃的 and 是不能吃的.

corrections.before: 因为他们吃了毒
corrections.after: 因为他们吃的植物有毒
corrections.explanation: The intended meaning is that the plants they ate were poisonous. Say that the plants have poison, rather than saying they ate poison.

corrections.before: 有一个老人叫神农，他什么植物都觉得好吃
corrections.after: 有一个老人叫神农，什么植物都觉得好吃
corrections.explanation: After introducing 神农 in the same sentence, omit the repeated subject pronoun. The omitted subject still clearly refers to 神农.

corrections.before: 他们还怕吃毒
corrections.after: 他们还怕中毒
corrections.explanation: 中毒 means “to be poisoned.” 怕吃毒 does not express the intended meaning naturally.

expressiveness.where: 他希望别人也可以吃好吃的植物
expressiveness.idea: You could add Shennong’s thought that everyone should know which plants are safe to eat.
expressiveness.example: 他想：大家应该知道什么植物能吃。

expressiveness.where: 可是他知道，如果他们还怕吃毒，不会吃他喜欢的植物
expressiveness.idea: You could show his decision to test plants himself so that he can help other people.
expressiveness.example: 所以，他决定自己试一试各种植物。

scenes.encouragement: You clearly explain the problem people faced with plants and give Shennong a kind reason for wanting to help them. The contrast with “可是” also makes his motivation easy to follow.

scenes.text: 所以，他上山下山找植物，吃了很多样子的植物。他是第一人，找到了茶。他把所有的植物写下来了。他一直都吃了，他连毒都能吃。可是他还没吃了一个叫夹竹桃的植物。他找到了那个像星星的植物，觉得很漂亮，马上就吃下了。

corrections.before: 吃了很多样子的植物
corrections.after: 吃了很多种植物
corrections.explanation: 样子 means appearance. Use 种 to count different kinds of plants.

corrections.before: 他是第一人，找到了茶
corrections.after: 他是第一个找到茶的人
corrections.explanation: To say someone was the first person to do an action, use 第一个 + verb + 的人.

corrections.before: 他一直都吃了
corrections.after: 他一直都在吃
corrections.explanation: 一直 describes an action continuing over time, so use 在 to show the ongoing action. Do not use 了 here.

corrections.before: 他连毒都能吃
corrections.after: 他连有毒的植物都能吃
corrections.explanation: 毒 is poison, not the plant that he eats. Say 有毒的植物 for poisonous plants.

corrections.before: 可是他还没吃了一个叫夹竹桃的植物
corrections.after: 可是他还没吃过一种叫夹竹桃的植物
corrections.explanation: 了 cannot be used after 没. Use 没吃过 to say that he had not tried it, and use 种 for a kind of plant.

corrections.before: 找到了那个像星星的植物
corrections.after: 找到那个像星星的植物
corrections.explanation: In this series of actions, only the final action takes 了. The final verb 吃下了 already shows that the actions were completed.

expressiveness.where: 他找到了那个像星星的植物，觉得很漂亮，马上就吃下了
expressiveness.idea: You could add that the flowers were yellow to make the plant easier to picture.
expressiveness.example: 花是黄色的。

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show Shennong’s active work with the vivid phrase “上山下山找植物.” You also include important story steps: finding tea, writing about plants, and then discovering the star-like plant.

scenes.text: 可是夹竹桃的毒很重，让他肚子很痛。他在地上躺着，觉得他快会死了。可是正好有别人找到他了，给了他一个像伞的植物，叫灵芝。他吃灵芝以后就觉得很好，不再生病了。他测量起来了，像星星的植物是毒，像伞的植物是药。

corrections.before: 觉得他快会死了
corrections.after: 觉得快要死了
corrections.explanation: The person who feels this is also the person who is about to die, so do not repeat 他 here. Use 快要 to say that something is about to happen.

corrections.before: 正好有别人找到他了
corrections.after: 正好有人找到他
corrections.explanation: Use 有人 for an unspecified person. 别人 means “other people” and needs a clear group that they are other than.

corrections.before: 吃灵芝以后
corrections.after: 吃了灵芝以后
corrections.explanation: Eating the lingzhi is completed before the next event, so use 了 with 吃.

corrections.before: 像星星的植物是毒
corrections.after: 像星星的植物有毒
corrections.explanation: Use 有毒 to say that a plant is poisonous. 是毒 is not the usual way to express this.

vocabulary_suggestions.note: “疼” is a more natural everyday word for a physical ache in the stomach.

expressiveness.where: 可是正好有别人找到他了
expressiveness.idea: You could describe the helper’s blue clothes to make this person easier for the listener to picture.
expressiveness.example: 那个人穿着蓝色的衣服。

expressiveness.where: 他吃灵芝以后就觉得很好，不再生病了
expressiveness.idea: You could add a short question from Shennong to show that he wants to learn about the helpful plant.
expressiveness.example: 神农问：“这是什么植物？”

scenes.encouragement: You clearly show the important cause-and-effect sequence: the oleander hurts Shennong, and lingzhi helps him feel better. You also contrast the star-shaped poisonous plant with the umbrella-shaped medicinal plant well.
